papers.title: Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent Architecture for Traceable, Risk-Aware Human-AI Decision Support in Manufacturing
papers.abstract: High-precision CNC machining of free-form aerospace components requires bounded compensations informed by inspection, simulation, and process knowledge. Off-the-shelf large language model (LLM) assistants can generate text, but they do not reliably execute risk-constrained multi-step numerical workflows or provide auditable provenance for high-stakes decisions. We present multi-agent knowledge analysis (MAKA), a human-in-the-loop decision-support architecture that separates intent routing, tools-only quantitative analysis, knowledge graph retrieval, and critic-based verification that enforces physical plausibility, safety bounds, and provenance completeness before recommendations are surfaced for human approval. MAKA is instantiated on a Ti-6Al-4V rotor blade machining testbed by fusing virtual-machining path-tracking error fields, cutting-force and deflection simulations, and scan-based 3D inspection deviation maps from 16 blades. The analysis decomposes deviation into an evidence-linked pathing component, a drift-based wear proxy capturing systematic evolution across parts, a residual systematic compliance term, and a variability proxy for instability-aware escalation. In a three-level tool-orchestration benchmark (single-step through $\geq$3-step stateful sequences), MAKA improves successful tool execution by up to 87.5 percentage points relative to an unstructured single-model interaction pattern with identical tool access. Digital twin what-if studies show MAKA can coordinate traceable compensation candidates that reduce predicted surface deviation from order $10^{-2}$in to approximately $\pm 10^{-3}$in over most of the blade within the simulation environment, providing a pre-deployment verification signal for risk-aware human decision-making.

summary_en.motivation: To improve precision and safety in high-stakes CNC machining of free-form aerospace components.
summary_en.method: A human-in-the-loop multi-agent architecture that separates intent routing, tools-only quantitative analysis, knowledge graph retrieval, and critic-based verification.
summary_en.result: The architecture improves successful tool execution by up to 87.5 percentage points over a baseline, and reduces predicted surface deviation to approximately ±10^-3 inches.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation on 16 Ti-6Al-4V rotor blades combined with digital twin simulations.

papers.title: Dissimilar friction stir welding of Ti-64 and Ti-407: Microstructural and mechanical evolutions
papers.abstract: Dissimilar joining of titanium alloys with different microstructure, chemical composition and mechanical properties offers considerable potential for optimising structural performance and reducing costs in aerospace and lightweight engineering applications. In this work, Ti-6Al-4V (Ti-64) and the recently developed Ti-407 alloy were successfully joined using stationary shoulder friction stir welding (SS-FSW), with Ti-64 placed on the advancing side (AS) and Ti-407 on the retreating side (RS). Comprehensive microstructural, textural, and mechanical characterisations of the parent materials and weld regions were conducted using scanning electron microscopy, electron backscatter diffraction, uniaxial tensile testing, low-cycle fatigue testing, and high-resolution nanoindentation mapping. The weld nugget exhibited a fully martensitic microstructure with refined prior-β grains and a near-random crystallographic texture. In contrast, the thermo-mechanically affected zones (TMAZs) displayed pronounced asymmetry between the advancing and retreating sides. The Ti-64/Ti-407 SS-FSW weld zone showed reduced tensile strength and a significant loss of ductility, attributed to strain localisation within the stir zone. Despite this tensile strength reduction, the weld zone demonstrated low-cycle fatigue lives comparable to, or exceeding, those of both parent alloys, owing to its fine martensitic microstructure, which delayed crack initiation and arrested the crack. Nanoindentation mapping revealed sharp hardness gradients across the weld, whereas elastic modulus variations were comparatively smooth, indicating that plastic deformation behaviour is more sensitive to local microstructural refinement than elastic response. Overall, these results demonstrate that robust cyclic performance can be achieved in dissimilar titanium welded components despite reduced tensile properties. The study confirms that SS-FSW is an effective joining technique for dissimilar Ti-64 and Ti-407 alloy parts; however, heterogeneous microstructural evolution within the weld zone plays a critical role in governing the mechanical performance of the welded parts.

summary_zh.method: 采用静止轴肩搅拌摩擦焊连接Ti-64和Ti-407，并进行微观结构和力学表征
summary_zh.result: 焊接区因细马氏体组织表现出优良的低周疲劳性能

summary_en.motivation: To explore the potential of dissimilar titanium alloy joining via friction stir welding for aerospace applications.
summary_en.method: Stationary shoulder friction stir welding was used to join Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-407, followed by microstructural and mechanical characterization.
summary_en.result: The weld zone exhibited excellent low-cycle fatigue life due to fine martensitic microstructure despite reduced tensile strength.
summary_en.validation: Validation through tensile tests, low-cycle fatigue tests, and nanoindentation mapping.
